title: Guinea-Bissau intercepts 168 would-be migrants over three days
description: Guinea-Bissau’s National Guard intercepted 168 migrants attempting the perilous journey to Europe via the Atlantic Ocean over recent days. The route is known for its danger but remains a common path for migrants.

title: Top Arab-Israeli leader tells AFP opposition must join to oust Netanyahu
description: Yousef Jabareen, leader of the Joint List, urges opposition parties to unite to challenge Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following inconclusive election results.

description: LONDON: A fire broke out on Monday at a warehouse storing fireworks in Jouret El-Ballout, near Broummana in Lebanon’s northern Metn district, triggering explosions and sending thick plumes of smoke over the area, local media reported. The smoke was visible from surrounding areas, including near Dbayeh, as firefighters rushed to the scene. description: LONDON: Britain's Labour party said Monday it had ended cooperation and power-sharing arrangements with the Greens in 11 English local authorities after the smaller left-wing party adopted a motion defining “Zionism as racism.” Members of the Greens, which has five MPs in Britain's 650-seat parliament and has enjoyed a boost in recent local and special elections, backed the motion at the party's annual conference last month. title: Floods inundate farmland in eastern Syria, damage crops
description: LONDON: Floodwaters in the Syrian Arab Republic submerged about 2.5 sq. km of farmland in Deir Ezzor and damaged crops in neighboring Raqqa, where preliminary assessments showed losses exceeding 40 percent in some maize fields, agricultural officials said. title: Schooling for nearly 80,000 students disrupted by Israeli military operation in Hebron, union says
description: LONDON: Nearly 80,000 Palestinian students missed school last week amid an Israeli military operation in Hebron, the General Union of Palestinian Teachers said, shortly before an Israeli military official confirmed on Monday that troops had withdrawn from the occupied West Bank city. title: Israeli authorities demolish house in Shefa-Amr amid rising Arab home demolitions
description: Israeli authorities demolished a house in Shefa-Amr for alleged illegal construction, amidst a rise in demolitions across Arab-majority towns in Israel. The demolished house belonged to Safiya Hajirat and housed four family members, with several other homes in the area under threat. The recent trends highlight ongoing tensions regarding housing and land ownership among Israel's Arab citizens.

title: UNRWA’s Gaza employees march against job cuts
description: UNRWA employees in Gaza staged a march to protest anticipated job cuts by the agency. The demonstration highlights concerns over reduced services for Palestinian refugees.

description: Kyiv now needs roughly twice as many jammers to stop each upgraded Shahed, intel officials and experts said.

description: The missiles — which are yet to be manufactured — are not expected to be delivered until a couple of years into the 2030s.

title: Tiny Ukrainian receiver intercepts Russian drone feeds in real time
description: A small new receiver can co-opt video from Russian unmanned systems, allowing Ukrainian drone operators to intercept enemy live feeds in real time, the device's makers said this month.

title: Ukraine and Russia report fake emergency alerts after cyberattacks target apps
description: Authorities in Ukraine and Russia said their emergency alert mobile apps had been targeted by cyberattacks, with users in Ukraine receiving false warnings of an imminent nuclear threat. Moscow said that hackers had sent fake emergency alerts after gaining access to the Russian Emergency Situations Ministry’s mobile app, and that efforts were ongoing to restore the app's functionality.

title: French school protests resume on smaller scale after autumn break
description: French high school student protests resumed on Monday on a ​much smaller scale than in past weeks as pupils returned from a two-week break, with youngsters trying to blockade a few high schools in Paris, Marseille and Rennes.

title: A musical overview of trans-European punk
description: This week on arts24, we're bringing you a double dose of European punk. Elias Bender Rønnenfelt is a singer with Copenhagen's finest post-punk export, Iceage. The group is currently touring Europe, and he is stopping off in Paris this week to play the Pitchfork festival solo. We also welcome Chris Hughes from Fat Dog. title: Israel's president begins process of coalition government negotiations
description: Israel's President Isaac Herzog begins the process of coalition government negotiations this week. One possibility is for the centrist opposition bloc to form a government with the Arab parties, which would oust current Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Protests for and against such a coalition this weekend made it clear the Israeli public is divided over the idea.

title: Iran offers deal on Hormuz Strait, Netanyahu wants to 'finish the job'
description: Iran said Monday it had a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks with the United States, shortening a process originally expected to take seven days. Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he wanted to "finish the job" first. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley has more.

title: Iran engages US in 'intensive' negotiations to avert fresh war outbreak
description: Tehran on Monday said that the country was holding "intensive" indirect talks with Washington to avoid a fresh round of US attacks on Iran ahead of the US midterm elections this week. Foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei shared Iranian plans to reopen blockaded energy corridor, the Strait of Hormuz, if the US were to meet its demands.

title: Jerusalem Daily: Israel’s lockdown of Hebron comes to an end
description: Israeli forces ended their lockdown of Hebron in the occupied West Bank, but its forces continued to attack a school.

title: China steps up Middle East diplomacy with Iran and Oman meetings
description: Beijing urges dialogue on US-Iran war, sends envoy to Gulf as Xi hosts first Omani head of state visit since 1978.
